data.name: Jard
data.long_meaning: In the ancient Greek language, Jard is derived from the root word 'jardos' which means 'to deceive' or 'to supplant'. This name was often given to a child born out of wedlock, or to a child who was expected to take the place of an older sibling. In the Bible, there is a figure named Jared who lived for an exceptionally long time, and this name may also be inspired by his story.
